text:
The stock barely moved today despite oil prices falling on easing Middle East tensions. Yesterday oil traders were pricing in a risk of Iranian supply disruptions, which pushed U.S. crude to higher levels and lifted the stock 2.3% on October 28th. Today's news about renewed U.S.-Iran peace efforts removed that supply-shock premium from oil prices, which typically would pressure an oil company's stock downward—but the move was so small it barely registered.

The stock's real story this week is the 5.2% two-week rally, which rode the wave of supply-threat concerns that now appear to be fading. Over the past day and a half, as tensions eased, the stock has given back some of those geopolitical gains, falling 1.5% from its October 26th high. Whether this pullback settles into a new level or bounces back depends on whether oil markets stay convinced the Middle East risks have truly passed.
